original.statement: MTU auto-detection is now continuous during agent lifetime; changing device MTU no longer requires restarting the agent to pick up the new MTU.

exposure.needed: whether the environment relies on Cilium MTU auto-detection (rather than an explicitly configured MTU) and changes network device MTUs while the agent is running; the release notes name no configuration key for this

corrected.statement: MTU auto-detection is now continuous during the agent's lifetime, so changing a device MTU no longer requires restarting the agent to pick up the new MTU. Exposed environments are those that rely on MTU auto-detection and change device MTUs while the agent is running. No static configuration key named in the evidence shows this.

decision.reason: [ev-01a5226ddc9a] says only that MTU auto-detection now runs continuously during the agent's lifetime, so a device MTU change no longer needs an agent restart. It does not tie exposure to any Kubernetes kind, so "gvk-in-use Deployment" is the wrong condition: it would flag nearly every cluster and has nothing to do with MTU. Exposure depends on two things: whether the environment relies on MTU auto-detection, and whether device MTUs change while the agent is running. The evidence names no configuration key for either, and the second is runtime behaviour, so the honest condition is undecidable.
